title: The Vibrating Crystal Inside Every Wristwatch

scenes.narration: Your watch doesn't tick using gears or microchips to keep time. It uses a microscopic tuning fork carved from quartz rock.
scenes.objective: Hook viewer with the surprise that a rock keeps time.

scenes.narration: Quartz exhibits the piezoelectric effect: apply voltage and it bends; release voltage and it produces an electric pulse.
scenes.objective: Show the piezoelectric bend and voltage pulse.

scenes.narration: Engineers carve this crystal so precisely that a watch battery makes it oscillate at exactly thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight times per second.
scenes.objective: Reveal the precise 32,768 Hz resonance driven by the battery.
keywords: thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight times per second

scenes.narration: Why this number? Because thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight equals two to the fifteenth power.
Fifteen flip-flop dividers halve that frequency fifteen times, producing exactly one pulse per second.
scenes.objective: Show the cascade division from 32 kHz to 1 Hz.

scenes.narration: That single pulse advances the second hand one tick.
scenes.objective: Show the stepper motor driving the gear train to move the second hand.

scenes.narration: A stone crystal vibrating thirty-two thousand times a second measures human time with near-atomic precision.
scenes.objective: Final pull-out revealing the complete watch keeping perfect time.
